prompt: Please review the account-deletion design in docs/design/account-deletion.md before we take it to the architecture review. This is time-sensitive because the consumer app is preparing its regional rollout, and I need confidence that the proposed behavior is implementable, meets the commitments in the packet, and can be operated when dependencies are unavailable. Read the supporting files in the packet rather than judging the design in isolation. Call out concrete contradictions, missing behavior, unsafe assumptions, and unclear ownership that could affect users or the teams running this service. Keep the review focused on issues a developer or service owner can act on, and include the consequence in this project. Write the review to REVIEW.md at the top of the project. End it with a fenced json list of findings, each with location (the section number of the document, like 3.2), severity (critical, high, medium, low or nit), issue and fix.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const H=new Set();for(const l of fs.readFileSync("docs/design/account-deletion.md","utf8").split("\n")){const m=l.match(/^#+\s*(?:section\s*)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/i);if(m)H.add(m[1])}process.exit(L.every(x=>{const m=String(x.location).match(/\d+(?:\.\d+)*/);return m&&H.has(m[0])})?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Each important finding explains a concrete consequence in this project and gives a fix a developer or service owner can act on, without inventing problems unsupported by the packet (code cannot check this because it requires judging meaning, evidence, and actionability).

findingsKey.finding: The design calls the request complete while encrypted snapshots and object manifests remain under a 90-day policy, so account data can survive the deletion process in recovery copies.
The plan does not issue or verify deletion of the account's warehouse rows even though the inventory identifies the analytics warehouse as a retained account-level copy.
The asynchronous flow can mark work complete after worker acknowledgement without an end-to-end completion check or a reliable report proving every system finished.
The evidence record retains the deleted person's email address and display name even though the legal requirements call for minimum evidence using a request reference and account identifier.
The design leaves the notification provider's recipient and delivery data in place because the worker does not invoke the vendor removal contract.
The design promises 30 business days and pauses for holidays, which conflicts with the 30-calendar-day legal deadline and can make a request late.

items.text: Explains how concurrent account writes, delayed events, and already-created exports are fenced so a late producer cannot recreate or expose data after deletion begins.
Asks for an explicit abuse and takeover analysis of the verification flow, including rate limits, reauthentication, and operator authorization for requests and holds.
items.source: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org (CC BY-SA 4.0)

items.text: Asks how the service sheds load when Search, storage, or another dependency slows down, which work is dropped or deferred first, and how that choice affects the deadline.
Requests a clear fencing or lease-expiry design for two workers processing one message, rather than relying only on idempotency records to prevent stale work.
Calls for an access review and key-rotation plan for the restricted evidence database and deletion logs, including who can export evidence and how that access is detected.
items.source: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org (CC BY-SA 4.0)

items.text: Asks whether deployment configuration such as replica caps, queue names, and provider endpoints is injected per environment instead of being coupled to the application artifact.

weakAnswers: The design is clear and well structured, with good state names and a reasonable rollout.
Consider scalability and monitoring as traffic grows.
The queue, retries, and idempotency approach should be tested thoroughly.
The proposal uses existing services and keeps the user experience asynchronous.

verdicts.note: Prompt does not name review method, checklist, planted problems, or count
Clear instructions: review docs/design/account-deletion.md, write REVIEW.md with section numbers, severity, issue, fix
Quick review misses legal deadline, warehouse, evidence fields, vendor, queue-ack completion
All six key items are verifiable at listed sections with defendable severity
No fixture file, comment, test, or name points at planted problems
